purpose: Add a generation x MW x rental-rate x annual-revenue curve and connect it to the MW/$ time axis without replacing canonical recognized-revenue/effective-MW accounting.
key_findings: DB deal estimates put the visible SpaceX hosting curve at roughly $31-$61M per compute MW-year, with GB300 deals near $50-$61M/MW-year.
DB's Colossus II phase table repeatedly uses 500 GB300 GPUs per labeled compute MW, or 2.0kW/GPU on that perimeter.
The displayed five-customer hosting total is $54.504B and the figure says roughly 1.2-1.4GW is allocated, implying about $40-$45B/GW blended.
The visible deal rows themselves total 1,175MW and about $54.505B, implying $46.4M/MW-year; this is not the same denominator as the blended-rate estimate.
Short- versus long-duration hosting ranges support a time-scarcity hypothesis but do not identify one exact time premium because ranges overlap and contracts differ.
This material narrows the forward-contract monetization gap but does not resolve SpaceX's canonical recognized revenue per effective utilized IT MW.
strongest_disconfirming_fact: SpaceX's filed Q2 recognized new-cloud revenue divided by total modeled average nameplate capacity remains only $4.57-$6.40M/MW-year, and filings still do not disclose external allocation, physical utilization or PUE.
